business_model.claim: Grupo Aval is a Colombian banking group that earns money from lending, deposit-taking, and pension and severance fund management.
quotes: we are Colombia’s largest banking group based on consumer loans and leading in payroll loans
We provide a comprehensive range of financial services and products from traditional banking services, such as making loans and taking deposits, to pension and severance fund management.

business_model.basis: stated in P2 and P3; the segment framing is inferred from the risk-factor headings and the MD&A wording
business_model.claim: The group is built from distinct business lines: commercial banks, a pension and severance fund administrator, and a merchant bank (Corficolombiana). The filing discusses a banking segment and a merchant banking segment.
quotes: Our principal subsidiaries in Colombia are financial institutions (four commercial banks, a pension and severance fund administrator and a merchant bank), and the majority of our operations, properties and customers are located in Colombia.

business_model.basis: stated in the F1 balance sheet and F2 income statement
business_model.claim: Lending is the core earning asset. Interest on the loan portfolio was 22,463,395 (table in millions of COP) of total interest income of 25,919,198 (table in millions of COP). Gross loans were 192,655,943 (table in millions of COP), made up of commercial 108,308,984, consumer 60,456,213 and mortgages 22,111,710 (table in millions of COP).
Net interest income rose to 7,871,331 (table in millions of COP) from 6,927,411 because interest expense, (18,047,867) from (20,044,491), fell by more than interest income.
quotes: Total interest expense decreased 10.0% or Ps 1,996.6 billion, more than total interest income, resulting from a 156-basis points reduction in interest rates paid on interest-bearing liabilities, partially offset by a 9.3% or Ps 20,991.2 billion increase in the average balance of interest-bearing liabilities.

business_model.claim: The margin is sensitive to interest rates because of the balance sheet structure. Mostly fixed-rate retail loans represent 43.3% of total loans, while 35.7% of local currency deposits come from institutional clients that reprice quickly.
quotes: which represent 43.3% of our total loans and are mostly fixed rate

our deposit structure continues to be sensitive to benchmark interest rate movements, where 35.7% of our local currency deposits come from institutional clients (financial institutions and government entities) and have a higher pass-through of movements in benchmark rates.

business_model.claim: Customer deposits are the main funding source: 207,405,238 (table in millions of COP) in total, including savings accounts of 88,238,541 and time deposits of 95,105,917. Bonds issued were 21,456,986. Interest paid on deposits was (13,089,554), the largest interest expense line.

Fees are a second revenue stream. Net income from commissions and fees was 3,660,045 (table in millions of COP) against 3,475,979 the year before. Growth was led by pension and severance fund management and banking fees.
quotes: Net income from commissions and fees grew 5.3% during the year, driven by a strong fees performance of pension and severance fund management and banking and other fees, which increased 9.1% and 3.9%, respectively.

business_model.claim: Non-financial businesses held through the merchant bank add a separate revenue line. Income from sales of goods and services was 10,396,794 (table in millions of COP) against costs of (8,309,074), leaving gross profit of 2,087,720, down from 2,477,355. The merchant banking segment carries far more interest-bearing liabilities than interest-earning assets.
quotes: The merchant banking segment inherently has significantly more interest-bearing liabilities than interest-earning assets, as a result of a substantial portion of funding used to finance both the ordinary course of non-financial businesses and Corficolombiana’s investment portfolio in debt and equity securities.

business_model.basis: stated in F1, F2 and P3
business_model.claim: Credit costs are a major cost driver. Net impairment losses were (3,538,900) (table in millions of COP) against (4,046,323) the year before, and the loss allowance on loans was (8,429,970). Cost of risk fell mainly because consumer loan quality improved.
quotes: Net cost of risk decreased 38 basis points in 2025 mainly driven by an improvement in the asset quality of consumer portfolio, while commercial loans slightly deteriorated.

business_model.claim: Operating expenses are the other large cost. Other expenses were (8,899,891) (table in millions of COP) against (8,125,461) the year before. The cost-to-income ratio improved to 52.2% from 53.2%.
quotes: Cost metrics evidence adequate expense management during the year, with cost to assets remaining relatively stable and cost to income decreasing 101 bps to 52.2% for 2025 compared to 53.2% for 2024.

business_model.basis: stated in F2; the consolidation mechanism is inferred
business_model.claim: Only part of consolidated profit accrues to Grupo Aval shareholders. Of net income for the year of 3,215,172 (table in millions of COP), 1,721,872 belongs to owners of the parent and 1,493,300 to non-controlling interests.
Foreign exchange affects the business, though foreign currency loans and deposits are a minority of the book: 8.7% of loans and 7.8% of deposits.
quotes: At December 31, 2025, 8.7% of our loans and 7.8% of our deposits were denominated in foreign currency.

business_model.basis: stated in F1, P1 and P3
business_model.claim: The group is reshaping its perimeter. The Panama unit MFG is shown as a discontinued operation and held for sale, with non-current assets held for sale of 18,256,613 (table in millions of COP) against 105,214. Banco de Bogotá also announced the purchase of Itaú’s retail banking operations in Colombia and Panama.
quotes: On March 18, 2026, following the receipt of all required regulatory authorizations, the sale of MFG to BIC was completed.
On December 23, 2025, Banco de Bogotá announced the acquisition of Itaú’s retail banking operations in Colombia and Panama

business_model.claim: Taxes weigh on profit: the income tax rate for financial institutions such as Grupo Aval and its banks is temporarily higher at 40%. Income tax expense was (1,432,708) (table in millions of COP) on pre-tax income of 4,621,234.
quotes: such rate will be temporarily higher (40%), from 2023 to 2027

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (company's own description in the 20-F); no independent ranking source in the packet
competitive_position.claim: Grupo Aval describes itself as Colombia's largest banking group by consumer loans, leader in payroll loans, and first in term deposits and checking accounts. This is the company's own ranking, stated as of year-end 2025.
quotes: we are Colombia’s largest banking group based on consumer loans and leading in payroll loans
we rank first in term deposits and checking accounts

competitive_position.claim: Total loan market share was 25.0% at the end of 2025, 28 basis points lower than in 2024. Consumer loan share was 28.9%, down 53 basis points. The lead is large but eroded slightly in 2025.
quotes: As a result of the abovementioned, we closed our market share in total loans at 25.0%, 28 basis points lower than in 2024.
Overall, our market share for consumer loans closed at 28.9%, with a 53 basis points decrease.

competitive_position.claim: Payroll lending leadership is intact, but the share fell. Aval holds a 42.2% payroll market share after a 127 bps reduction, as it diversified toward higher-yielding, shorter-term consumer loans.
quotes: All of this, while maintaining our leadership position in payroll lending, where we have a 42.2% market share, where we reduced our share by 127 bps.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items (management commentary)
competitive_position.claim: Aval gained deposit share among individuals and grew total deposits in 2025, supporting its funding franchise.
quotes: We prioritized individuals’ deposits and we succeeded in 2025 by reaching +71bp of market share gain across banks.
Total deposits grew 11.2% in 2025

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items; mechanism stated by management
competitive_position.claim: Profitability recovered strongly in 2025. Net income attributable to owners rose 69.6% and return on average equity reached 9.6% against 6.0% in 2024. Management attributes this mainly to a recovery in net interest margin from lower funding costs.
quotes: Net income attributable to owners of the parent increased 69.6% to Ps 1,721.9 billion, compared to Ps 1,015.1 billion in 2024.
Return on average equity for 2025 was 9.6% as compared to 6.0% in 2024.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items (statement and MD&A)
competitive_position.claim: Net interest income rose while interest expense fell more than interest income. This shows funding-cost advantage and repricing in 2025 rather than balance-sheet shrinkage.
quotes: Total interest expense decreased 10.0% or Ps 1,996.6 billion, more than total interest income

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items; the loss allowance figures (COP millions: 8,429,970 in 2025, 10,006,639 in 2024) come from the balance sheet table
competitive_position.claim: Asset quality improved, reducing the cost of defending the loan book. Loans more than 90 days past due fell to 3.3%, and the loss allowance on the balance sheet fell.
quotes: Loans past due more than 90 days were 3.3% at December 31, 2025, 77 basis points lower compared to December 31, 2024.

competitive_position.claim: Pension and severance management (Porvenir) is a strong segment. Management reports record annual performance, with ROAE of 21.2% and assets under management of Ps 271.2 trillion, up 14.9%.
quotes: Porvenir delivered its strongest annual performance to date.

competitive_position.basis: inferred from the income statement and balance sheet figures (COP millions); the interpretation is not stated in the filing
competitive_position.claim: Aval's earnings are shared with minorities. Net income attributable to non-controlling interests was 1,493,300 against 1,721,872 to owners of the parent (COP millions, 2025), and non-controlling interests are 16,296,936 of equity versus 18,445,905 for owners. Only part of the group's earning power accrues to Grupo Aval shareholders.

Pricing pressure in large-corporate commercial lending is a named competitive threat. Aval lost 204 basis points of share there and chose to be selective. Its USD commercial loan share fell 356 bps to 35.3%.
quotes: We are selective in large corporate commercial loans, given the aggressive pricing competition present throughout the year, where we lost 204 basis points.

competitive_position.basis: share loss stated in P3; competition risk stated in the P2 risk summary
competitive_position.claim: Credit cards face high competition. Aval's card market share closed at 17.4% after giving up 132bps, even as it launched the FIFA-VISA alliance.
quotes: we are exposed to high competition in the credit card industry

competitive_position.claim: The balance-sheet structure is a named vulnerability to interest-rate cycles. Retail products are mostly fixed-rate and 35.7% of local-currency deposits come from institutional clients who reprice quickly. Funding costs can therefore rise faster than loan yields when rates rise.
quotes: The characteristics of retail products (mainly consumer and mortgages) in the local market, which represent 43.3% of our total loans and are mostly fixed rate, has made it difficult to immediately or fully pass through higher interest rates to our customers.
This balance sheet structure results in the cost of interest-bearing liabilities increasing faster than interest income on loans.

competitive_position.claim: The Colombian macro and political backdrop is a named threat. S&P Global Ratings downgraded Colombia's sovereign ratings, the 2025 fiscal deficit was 6.4% of GDP, and the filing cites inflation above the Central Bank target.
quotes: On April 8, 2026, S&P Global Ratings downgraded Colombia’s long-term foreign currency sovereign credit rating to ‘BB-’ from ‘BB’, and its long-term local currency rating to ‘BB’ from ‘BB+’.
On the fiscal front, the deficit for 2025 closed at 6.4% of GDP and remains the main challenge of the country’s economy.

competitive_position.claim: Tax and regulatory policy is a named threat. Financial institutions such as Aval face a temporarily higher income tax rate, and the filing cites mandatory investment requirements and other government measures.
quotes: In the case of financial institutions, such as Grupo Aval and our banking subsidiaries, such rate will be temporarily higher (40%), from 2023 to 2027.

competitive_position.claim: Aval is reshaping its portfolio. Banco de Bogotá announced the acquisition of Itaú's retail banking in Colombia and Panama, adding clients, loans and deposits, pending regulatory approval. Banco de Bogotá also agreed to sell its Panama unit MFG, which is classified as discontinued operations.
quotes: adding 277,000 clients with Ps. $6.5 trillion in loans and Ps. $4.1 trillion in deposits

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (management description)
competitive_position.claim: Digital initiatives are cited as support for the franchise. Aval registered more than 850,000 new customers through its digital offering dale!, and it launched GOU Payments for Colombia's instant payments ecosystem.
quotes: We registered more than 850,000 new customers through dale! which delivers an end-to-end digital experience for individuals and microbusinesses.

competitive_position.claim: A legal overhang at Corficolombiana was removed. A court dismissed the case after the DOJ deferred prosecution agreement obligations were satisfied, closing the U.S. proceedings covered by the agreement.
quotes: received today an order from the competent court dismissing the case.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet and cash flow statement.
financial_health.claim: Cash and cash equivalents stood at 19,354,710 (table in millions of COP) at year-end 2025, up from 16,998,859 in the prior year. This is the only liquidity stock the statements show directly.

The balance sheet is highly leveraged in the usual bank sense. Total liabilities were 314,193,836 (table in millions of COP) against total equity of 34,742,841 and total assets of 348,936,677. Of the equity, 18,445,905 belongs to the parent's owners and 16,296,936 to non-controlling interests.

Funding is mainly customer deposits, 207,405,238 (table in millions of COP), up from 200,872,177. Financial obligations were 68,671,586, down from 72,823,775. Bonds issued fell to 21,456,986 from 26,215,847.

financial_health.claim: Deposit funding is rate-sensitive. 35.7% of local-currency deposits come from institutional clients, who pass benchmark rate moves through faster. The 20-F says this raises the cost of liabilities faster than loan income when rates rise.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement.

financial_health.basis: Inferred from the cash flow line items.

Profit supports internal capital generation. Net income for the year was 3,215,172 (table in millions of COP). Of that, 1,721,872 went to owners of the parent and 1,493,300 to non-controlling interests. Net interest income was 7,871,331 after impairment charges of (3,538,900).

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement.
